For Learners and Reviewers

The studio fundamentals.

12 working skills · taught by name in Years 1 and 2 · shown in every highlight after

The rule12 fundamentals

The twelve working skills every learner has by the end of Year 2, whatever their concentration: the ability to make, keep, and show work. A Bachelor of Arts in Technology in its old sense — the arts as the things people make — with the artist-engineer's twist: the record, the file, the version, the database, and the showing are part of the craft, not an afterthought.

Each fundamental is taught once, by name, on a day whose arc row carries it (the "taught" field names the course and day; "mark" is a phrase that must appear in that day's one idea). Later courses assume it. A highlight that is expected to show it lists it on the course page and in the Portfolio.

Each course page lists the fundamentals its highlight is expected to show, and the Portfolio prints the same list under the highlight. The fundamentals are the shared floor; the work on top of them is each learner's own.

The image4 fundamentals
FundamentalTaught, by nameShown in the highlight of
Raster and vectorTell a bitmap from a vector and choose the right one: a photograph is a grid of pixels and has a size; a drawing is lines and curves and has none, so it scales clean. Export each in a format that keeps what it is.WKSP 101 · Day 12
Semester 1		WKSP 101, PHYS 120, ENGR 310, CAP 402
Size, resolution, formatKnow what an image is in numbers: pixels wide and high, pixels per inch for print, the file format and what it throws away. Make the web size and the print size from one original, and name which is which.MATH 210 · Day 1
Semester 3		MATH 210, WKSP 102, SIG 201, CAP 402
Color, on purposeName a color three ways (RGB, hex, and the one the printer wants), pick a small palette and keep it, and check that text reads against its ground. Light and paint mix differently; know which one you are working in.MATH 210 · Day 3
Semester 3		MATH 210, WKSP 102, ART 310, ART 410
Photographing the workPhotograph a thing so it reads: one light source, a plain ground, the camera square to the object, in focus, at a size that will survive the Portfolio. Three photographs and a sentence, every session.WKSP 101 · Day 4
Semester 1		WKSP 101, WKSP 102, WKSP 201, WKSP 202, ENGR 310, ENGR 320
Sound and the moving image3 fundamentals
FundamentalTaught, by nameShown in the highlight of
Recording clean soundRecord a voice or an instrument so it is usable: a quiet room, the microphone close, levels that never clip, a file that keeps the recording whole (WAV) and one that travels (MP3), named and dated.SIG 101 · Day 14
Semester 2		SIG 101, ART 330
Shooting a clipShoot a clip a stranger can watch: the phone steady, the frame chosen, the light in front of the subject, sound recorded on purpose, and the aspect ratio decided before the first take (16:9 for a screen, 9:16 for a feed).SIG 201 · Day 2
Semester 4		SIG 201, ART 320, CAP 402
The cut, and the exportCut clips into a piece: in and out points, a title card, a sound level that holds, and an export at a stated resolution and format with a poster frame, under a length you named before you started.SIG 201 · Day 3
Semester 4		SIG 201, ART 320, CAP 402
The record3 fundamentals
FundamentalTaught, by nameShown in the highlight of
Files, names, foldersKeep the work where you can find it in a year: one folder per course, names that say what a file is and when it was made, no "final-final", and a copy somewhere the laptop is not.WKSP 101 · Day 4
Semester 1		WKSP 101, CS 110, RHET 110
Versions and version controlNever overwrite a draft: keep every version, dated, so the distance between them can be seen. For code and for any text that changes, use version control: a commit is a dated decision with a sentence on it, and the log is the history a stranger can read.CS 110 · Day 15
Semester 1		CS 110, RHET 110, CS 120, CS 210
A table of the workKeep a record of every made thing as data: one row each, with the same fields every time (what, when, where it is, what it showed). A spreadsheet or a file of records is the smallest database; the Portfolio reads one like it.CS 110 · Day 10
Semester 1		CS 110, MATH 220, CAP 401
Showing2 fundamentals
FundamentalTaught, by nameShown in the highlight of
Type and layoutPut words and a picture on a page so they read: two typefaces at most, one size for the title and one for the rest, a margin, things lined up on a grid, and nothing that is there because the tool offered it. A placard, a flyer, a slide, a thumbnail are all this.WKSP 102 · Day 10
Semester 2		MATH 210, WKSP 102, SIG 201, CAP 402
Showing the workHang, play, or publish the work so a stranger meets it well: at reading height, in good light, with the placard beside it, the cover image chosen, and the Portfolio highlight filled in the week it is shown, not a year later.WKSP 102 · Day 14
Semester 2		WKSP 102, WKSP 202, WKSP 402, CAP 402
Status

A working framework, not an authorized degree. SDIT is in its founding phase and is not yet authorized to grant degrees; where authorization stands is published in full. The curriculum is open and free to take.
